samples.question: This picture is a simple daytime drawing on white paper: a blue page frame, one or more pale blue clouds, a yellow sun disk in the sky, a dark green ground line, a brown tree trunk with a green crown standing on that line, and one grey shadow shape lying on the ground and touching the foot of the trunk. The frame, the clouds, the crown and the ground line are fixed decoration and never indicate the answer. Compare only horizontal, left-right positions, measured against the trunk: the sun is on the left of the trunk when the yellow disk lies further left than the trunk and on the right otherwise, and the shadow is on the left of the trunk when the grey shape stretches from the foot of the trunk towards the left and on the right otherwise. The height of the sun, its size, the length and thickness of the grey shadow, the size of the tree, the number and placement of the clouds, the position of everything on the page and the exact shades of the colours all change from picture to picture and never indicate the answer. Answer from the shadow that is actually painted in this picture, not from the side a shadow would fall on in the real world. Is the painted grey shadow on the same side of the trunk as the yellow sun, or on the opposite side? Answer with exactly one of the words same or opposite.
